title: Understand Linux sound system layers
summary: Linux audio has several layers: kernel drivers (ALSA), user-space APIs, and optional sound servers like PipeWire or PulseAudio. A default Arch install includes ALSA; sound servers add features like mixing multiple apps.

steps.explain: ALSA is the kernel component providing drivers and lowest-level support for audio hardware. It is present in the stock kernel.
Sound servers like PipeWire or PulseAudio are optional user-mode processes that handle mixing multiple audio streams and advanced features. PipeWire is the default choice in many distributions.
